notes:
Lead is small-mid support SaaS (multi-tenant). Primary aim: use Hosted API for automated replies and short agent assist. Customer initially self-serve with sample traffic ~50 req/min during tests. Main pain: perceived latency variance hurting UX for EU customers. Key details captured below:

- Symptoms: average p95 ~600-900ms overall but 5-8s occasional tails during bursts; EU region shows +60-90ms over US for same request types.
- Environment: testing from Heroku and internal dev machines; not yet using streaming.
- Prompts: mixed templates, some include 6-8kb of context (past conversation) which likely increases token count; they append full conversation history each call.
- Customer thinks "timeout" setting is default 30s — asked whether client-side SDKs should set lower timeouts to surface failures faster.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — wants to keep hosted usage under $1k/month initially.
- Model preference: open to smaller/faster model family for short replies; asked about recommended model variants and auto-fallback to cheaper models when response length is small.
- SE notes (Priya): try region comparison + short prompt experiment. Advise: pin model to small/fast for chat use-case, enable streaming to reduce TTF-first-byte, add prefix-trimming for history, and enable smart routing to closest region. Also recommend setting client timeout ~6-8s for UI calls and background retry for async tasks.
- Provided artifacts: quickstart deck, security mini-diagram, sample cURL traces and p95/p99 logs.
- Quote from call: "Users feel the typing pause — if it hits 2s it feels sluggish; anything above 4s and we see dropoff."

Next actions done/owned: Jordan to send perf checklist + sample curl commands; Priya to share region test script and recommended prompt truncation snippet; customer to run A/B for a week and share raw traces.

Notes: keep framing lightweight — SMB, likely converts to paid hosted API with gradual usage growth. No SOC2 required now; minimal audit logging requested. Will revisit Dedicated only if performance can't be achieved on hosted API.
